extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / wartime news consumers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and editorial coverage of active wartime operations and home-front effects for a general newspaper front page, combining dispatches, official communiqués, battlefield detail, and interpretive analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official communiqués and radio broadcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on and attribute official communiqués and radio broadcasts as primary sources (e.g., "The German high ... communique, broadcast by the Berlin radio and recorded by the Associated Press").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the issuing authority and medium (Berlin radio, Soviet midnight communique, Helsinki broadcast). Attribute claims clearly to their source so readers can weigh credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precise geographic and tactical details
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide place names, distances, and geographic features to situate actions (examples: Vadino; upper Donets River; Chuguev, 22 miles southeast of Kharkov; Bryansk; Novorossisk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include fronts, rivers, town distances and directional markers to help readers visualize movements and strategic context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report casualty and equipment counts (with source attribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish reported numbers of killed, captured, or destroyed personnel and matériel (e.g., "961 Soviet tanks...captured, destroyed, or disabled", "500 Russians had been killed", "542,000 men ... have been claimed from us in dead").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present such figures as claims with attribution; avoid presenting partisan counts as indisputable fact without corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present both sides' claims and note disagreements
rubrics_metrics.description: When opposing belligerents issue conflicting accounts (German claims vs. Soviet bulletins), print both and indicate differences (parenthetical notes like '(The Russians acknowledged...)' or '(The Germans had claimed...)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear which side is making each claim and, where possible, report corroborating or contradicting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe air and naval operations in operational detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover bombing raids, night vs. day operations, convoy attacks, and aircraft losses (examples: "Red bombers take toll", "British Whirlwind bombers...attacked 14 freight trains", "Two direct hits crippled the warship").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include type of aircraft/ships, mission profile (daylight or nocturnal), results observed, and tactical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include strategic implications and operational consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the strategic significance of actions (e.g., "The capture of Vadino...will afford the Red army a springboard for thrusts").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect battlefield events to likely next moves or broader campaign effects to give readers context beyond immediate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report home-front effects, material damage, and civilian impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe destruction and civilian consequences (e.g., Berlin: '30,000 were left homeless', '200 rooms in the Air Ministry demolished', '700 buildings damaged').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include estimates of casualties, homelessness, damaged infrastructure, and effects on production where available, with attribution to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover political leaders' speeches and propaganda as indicators of morale
rubrics_metrics.description: Report leaders' public statements and analyze propaganda for what they reveal about domestic morale (examples: Hitler's memorial day speech, Goebbels' propaganda, citation: 'the propaganda machine swung into action').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat speeches as both news and evidence; quote key lines and interpret what the rhetoric suggests about a nation's psychological state and policy aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide cautious editorial analysis and avoid over-reaching conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer interpretive commentary but warn against rash inferences (e.g., 'From this psychology it would be rash, however, to jump to the conclusion that Germany is near general collapse').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance interpretation with caveats about limited evidence; explain alternate readings and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include human-interest elements, awards, and personal anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Add stories about individuals, decorations, and ceremonial visits to humanize coverage (examples: awards to airmen; King's inspection of the fleet; anecdotes of pilots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brief personal details and quotations to provide color and connect readers to the human dimension of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name military units and commanders for specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify units and leaders when mentioned (e.g., '11th motorized infantry regiment of the ninth German tank division', 'Lieut.-Gen. Giffar Martel', 'General Eaker').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full unit and commander names help readers and researchers track developments; attribute reported actions to specific formations where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report logistics and infrastructure targets and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Note attacks on rail yards, viaducts, marshalling yards, shipyards, and supply lines (e.g., 'damaged the viaduct at Morlaix', 'railroad yards and loading installations...photographs show the main shipping and receiving area was knocked out').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the impact on an enemy's ability to sustain operations and include photographic or reconnaissance confirmation if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute photographic or reconnaissance confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use photographic evidence or observation to corroborate claims (example: 'Observations confirmed by photographs show the main shipping and receiving area was knocked out').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When photos or reconnaissance reports are cited, state their provenance and what they confirm to strengthen credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain tactical and training lessons where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Report doctrinal or training conclusions from commanders (e.g., 'the amount and state of training required for acceptable daylight bombing' learned by forces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include commanders' assessments about tactics, training, or equipment when they illuminate how operations will proceed or improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish reportage from propaganda when recounting enemy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When enemy sources make exaggerated or propagandistic statements (e.g., boasting of 'complete removal of all differences of classes' as a postwar promise), present them as claims and provide context or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label rhetorical or visionary statements as propaganda or ideology and, where useful, contrast them with observable facts or opposing viewpoints.
